info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package sandbox is the box scheduler: the control plane for the executor every other subsystem in this binary was already pointing at.

get.summary: Every box the caller's org holds
get.description: Lists this org's boxes with their class, status, project, image and volume. Filterable by project and status. Scoped to the caller's org by the validated identity, never by a value in the request.

post.description:
Claims an isolated execution box for the caller's org and returns it. A box is one pod running the box daemon with the project's volume attached: `exec` is a short-lived interpreter with no volume and no network, `dev` adds the project checkout and a toolchain, `desktop` adds a virtual display for computer use.

A claim comes from a WARM POOL where one is available, so the usual cost is a label patch and a volume attach rather than an image pull.

One live box per project: the project volume is single-attach, so a second concurrent claim is REFUSED with the id of the box already holding it rather than silently given an empty volume that reinstalls everything.

delete.description: Releases the pod. The project VOLUME is kept — it holds the checkout and the dependency caches, which is what makes the next claim fast. Pass purge=1 to drop the volume too; that is irreversible and deletes uncommitted work.

get.description: The box's current state, or 404 if this org does not hold it.

delete.description: The root of the box's project volume — list what is there, or write into it without naming a subpath. Same forwarding and same path confinement as the entries below it; this is the route for the directory itself, which a wildcard cannot address because there is no remainder to match.

delete.description:
Read, write, list, search and delete inside the box's project directory. Forwarded to the box daemon unchanged; the box resolves every path under the project root, so a path cannot address anything outside it.

NOTHING RUNS IN cloud. This is a proxy: boxes have no public address, and terminating auth anywhere but the IAM edge would mean a second auth path.

delete.summary: Clone into the box, or push what it changed
delete.description: Clones a repository into the box's project volume, or commits and pushes the branch the agent worked on. Git credentials travel in the request BODY only — never a URL, never a command line, never a log.

delete.summary: Run a command in the box
delete.description: Runs a command in the box's project directory and returns its exit code, stdout and stderr. A non-zero exit is a SUCCESSFUL call carrying a failed program — the HTTP status stays 200, because 'the tests failed' and 'the box is broken' are different facts.

post.description: Claims a pod and reattaches the project volume, optionally moving to a different git ref. The checkout and the caches are already on the disk.

post.summary: Suspend a box, keeping its disk
post.description: Releases the pod and keeps the volume, so a later resume is a fetch and a checkout rather than a clone and a cold install.
